newsitem.title: USA: WSCC okays 7,200 MW Pacific Intertie rating.
newsitem.headline: WSCC okays 7,200 MW Pacific Intertie rating.

text.p: The board of the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) said Friday it approved increasing the Pacific Intertie's capacity rating to 7,200 megawatts (MW) from a current rate of 6,250 MW.
The 7,200 MW operating level will be in effect until the Board endorses another change or until operating conditions no longer match the springtime conditions specified in the plan, the council said.

The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) had sought to increase the rating to 7,700 MW, but some utilities in the Southwest were opposed to any increase, which resulted in the compromise rate, sources involved in the talks said.
A BPA spokesman said just prior to official confirmation of the WSCC move that the agency was "ready to increase the lines whenever the WSCC gives us the go-ahead."
He noted line problems which in the past have delayed capacity increases were not a factor at this time.

The Intertie, which links the Pacific Northwest to Southern California, has a rated capacity of 7,900 MW, but was cut back to 5,200 MW amid reliability concerns following two power blackouts which hit the West last summer.
In late March, the WSCC approved increasing the line's capacity to 6,250 MW through the end of June.
